title: A parametrized status-code table that kills seven mutants
problem: app.py is a correct messages API with three endpoints: send (POST), list (GET with ?limit=1..100) and delete (DELETE) messages. Write its status-code table: grow CASES in test_api.py with one row per request, covering normal, invalid, edge and error paths of every endpoint, and write test_store_unavailable_is_503 with a dependency override. test_meta.py runs your table and test against seven broken copies of app.py.
requirements: Edit only test_api.py. Don't change app.py, conftest.py or test_meta.py
Keep the rows send-ok and list-ok; give every new row a readable id with pytest.param(..., id=...)
Rows are (method, url, json_body_or_None, expected_status) and must match the real app.py
Cover both sides of every boundary: limit and text length
test_store_unavailable_is_503 overrides get_store on client.app with a function that raises StoreUnavailable and asserts the 503 status and body
Derive rows from app.py first. Read the mutants in test_meta.py only after your first run
contract: test_api.py defines CASES: list of pytest.param(method, url, body, expected_status, id=...), test_status parametrized over CASES, and test_store_unavailable_is_503(client)
expectedBehavior: pytest -q shows every test_status[...] row, test_store_unavailable_is_503 and all seven test_tests_kill[...] cases passing
edgeCases: limit at 1 and 100 (valid) and at 0 and 101 (invalid)
A chat id that doesn't exist, on every endpoint
Deleting a message id that exists, but in another chat
The storage backend raising an exception
hints: Conceptual: go endpoint by endpoint and write the four kinds of path for each: normal, invalid, edge, error. Every number in app.py (ge=1, le=100, max_length=500, status_code=...) is a boundary that needs a row on each side.

Specific: the seeded data matters. Chat 1 has message 1 and chat 2 has none, so DELETE /chats/1/messages/1 is the 204 row, and DELETE /chats/2/messages/1 asks whether a message id from another chat is rejected. Don't forget an unknown chat id (9) for list and delete too.

Implementation: rows look like pytest.param("GET", "/chats/1/messages?limit=0", None, 422, id="list-limit-0") and pytest.param("POST", "/chats/1/messages", {"text": "x" * 501}, 422, id="send-501-chars"). For the 503 test, define a function that raises StoreUnavailable(), put it in client.app.dependency_overrides[get_store], then send any request and assert status and json().
evaluation: All tests pass, including the seven test_tests_kill cases
Each endpoint has normal, invalid, edge and error rows
Row ids say what the row checks
The 503 test uses dependency_overrides, not a change to app.py
